tier1.text: A muscular chamber between the esophagus and small intestine. It stores and mixes food with acid and enzymes before releasing it into the duodenum.

tier2.text: The stomach helps digest food from the esophagus, both mechanically and chemically, turning the food into chyme, a soupy liquid of food mixed with digestive juices. The stomach holds the chyme and releases it gradually into the small intestine through the pyloric sphincter, a muscle around the passage that acts as a valve. The only stomach function that is necessary for life is making intrinsic factor, which the intestine needs in order to absorb vitamin B12. The stomach lies between the liver and the spleen, under the diaphragm, the dome-shaped muscle beneath the lungs. The stomach has four main regions, the cardia, fundus, body and pylorus; food enters through the cardia, where the esophagus joins the stomach. Besides the usual circular and lengthwise muscle layers, the stomach wall has an inner oblique layer, running at an angle, that lets the stomach churn food vigorously and break it into smaller pieces. A vast number of gastric pits, narrow channels in the stomach lining, lead into gastric glands, which secrete a digestive fluid called gastric juice. The stomach's chief cells release pepsin, an enzyme (a protein that speeds up chemical reactions) that digests protein, in an inactive form called pepsinogen. Hydrochloric acid, a digestive acid secreted by the stomach's parietal cells, is needed to activate pepsin and also kills much of the bacteria swallowed with food. The stomach is kept from digesting itself by a mucosal barrier, which includes a thick coat of mucus whose bicarbonate neutralizes acid.

sentences.text: The stomach helps digest food from the esophagus, both mechanically and chemically, turning the food into chyme, a soupy liquid of food mixed with digestive juices.

quotes.quote: stomach: alimentary canal organ that contributes to chemical and mechanical digestion of food from the esophagus before releasing it, as chyme, to the small intestine
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: chyme: soupy liquid created when food is mixed with digestive juices
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The stomach holds the chyme and releases it gradually into the small intestine through the pyloric sphincter, a muscle around the passage that acts as a valve.

quotes.quote: The stomach begins the digestion of protein and continues the digestion of carbohydrates and fats. It stores food as an acidic liquid called chyme, and releases it gradually into the small intestine through the pyloric sphincter.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: Recall that sphincters are muscles that surround tubes and serve as valves, closing the tube when the sphincters contract and opening it when they relax.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The only stomach function that is necessary for life is making intrinsic factor, which the intestine needs in order to absorb vitamin B12.

quotes.quote: there is only one stomach function necessary to life: the production of intrinsic factor. The intestinal absorption of vitamin B12, which is necessary for both the production of mature red blood cells and normal neurological functioning, cannot occur without intrinsic factor.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The stomach lies between the liver and the spleen, under the diaphragm, the dome-shaped muscle beneath the lungs.

quotes.quote: It is located under the diaphragm, between the liver and the spleen as well as between the esophagus and the small intestine.
quotes.citation: NCI Thesaurus (NCIt), National Cancer Institute, https://ncithesaurus.nci.nih.gov

quotes.quote: diaphragm: domed-shaped skeletal muscle located under lungs that separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominal cavity
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The stomach has four main regions, the cardia, fundus, body and pylorus; food enters through the cardia, where the esophagus joins the stomach.

quotes.quote: There are four main regions in the stomach: the cardia, fundus, body, and pylorus (). The cardia (or cardiac region) is the point where the esophagus connects to the stomach and through which food passes into the stomach.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Besides the usual circular and lengthwise muscle layers, the stomach wall has an inner oblique layer, running at an angle, that lets the stomach churn food vigorously and break it into smaller pieces.

quotes.quote: In addition to the typical circular and longitudinal smooth muscle layers, the muscularis has an inner oblique smooth muscle layer (). As a result, in addition to moving food through the canal, the stomach can vigorously churn food, mechanically breaking it down into smaller particles.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: A vast number of gastric pits, narrow channels in the stomach lining, lead into gastric glands, which secrete a digestive fluid called gastric juice.

quotes.quote: A vast number of gastric pits dot the surface of the epithelium, giving it the appearance of a well-used pincushion, and mark the entry to each gastric gland, which secretes a complex digestive fluid referred to as gastric juice.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: gastric pit: narrow channel formed by the epithelial lining of the stomach mucosa
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The stomach's chief cells release pepsin, an enzyme (a protein that speeds up chemical reactions) that digests protein, in an inactive form called pepsinogen.

quotes.quote: Protein digestion is mediated by an enzyme called pepsin in the stomach chamber. Pepsin is secreted by the chief cells in the stomach in an inactive form called pepsinogen.
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: An enzyme is a catalytic protein that speeds up chemical reactions in the human body.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Hydrochloric acid, a digestive acid secreted by the stomach's parietal cells, is needed to activate pepsin and also kills much of the bacteria swallowed with food.

quotes.quote: HCl is responsible for the high acidity (pH 1.5 to 3.5) of the stomach contents and is needed to activate the protein-digesting enzyme, pepsin. The acidity also kills much of the bacteria you ingest with food and helps to denature proteins, making them more available for enzymatic digestion.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: hydrochloric acid (HCl): digestive acid secreted by parietal cells in the stomach
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The stomach is kept from digesting itself by a mucosal barrier, which includes a thick coat of mucus whose bicarbonate neutralizes acid.

quotes.quote: The stomach is protected from self-digestion by the mucosal barrier. This barrier has several components. First, the stomach wall is covered by a thick coating of bicarbonate-rich mucus. This mucus forms a physical barrier, and its bicarbonate ions neutralize acid.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
